---
title: "Hands-on: Measuring How Small the World Is"
---

You now know what average path length and clustering mean. Here you measure them, on generated networks where you know the answer and on a real one where you do not.

execute lives in a marimo notebook, so it stays interactive and reactive
instead of being a wall of output frozen into a web page.

## What you will build

1. Get comfortable with igraph: build graphs, compute shortest paths, extract components.
2. Compute local, average-local and global clustering, and reconcile them by hand on a small graph.
3. Generate lattices, random graphs and Watts-Strogatz networks, and compare them.
4. Compute the small-world index sigma against a random baseline.
5. Estimate path length by sampling when the network is too large for all-pairs.

## What to watch for

- Average local clustering and global clustering will disagree. Work out which nodes cause the gap before reading on.
- Sweep the rewiring probability p and plot clustering and path length together. The band where both are favourable is wider than most people guess.
